sources.entry: Bedrock Launcher - Play your own copy of Minecraft Bedrock Edition for Windows on Apple Silicon, fully offline, through a locally built WineGDK with DXMT. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon] ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]](https://github.com/pragyaangaur/Minecraft-Bedrock-macOS)

summary.one_liner: A macOS port toolkit that runs your own copy of Minecraft Bedrock Edition for Windows on Apple silicon Macs, offline, using a locally built WineGDK and DXMT.
summary.what_it_does: The project runs the Windows edition of Minecraft Bedrock that you already own on a Mac with an M1 chip or newer, and the README says it is the real game rather than a remake. It ships a launcher app (Bedrock Launcher) packaged as a disk image, but the download contains no game files: you copy the game folder and a memory dump of the running game from a Windows PC, and the app prepares the game on first launch. Tools in the repo rebuild the encrypted executable from the dump, restore its import table, and undo start-up state captured in the dump. Patches add to WineGDK (Xbox GDK runtime parts, a heap overrun fix, GameInput mouse support) and DXMT, and small stand-in DLLs replace the HTTP library so the game runs offline. Developers can run setup.sh to build GnuTLS, FreeType, WineGDK, LLVM 15 and DXMT from source and create a Wine prefix. The README reports survival, creative, the Nether and the End work, and that an M4 Mac runs it at about 100 fps.
use_cases: play my own Windows copy of Minecraft Bedrock on a Mac
run Minecraft offline on Apple silicon
build a Wine and DXMT game runtime from source
experiment with reverse engineering a Windows game binary for macOS
study WineGDK and DXMT patches for Xbox GDK games
launch a Windows game on macOS without a Windows install
how_to_run: Download Bedrock-Launcher.dmg, drag Bedrock Launcher into Applications, and allow it in System Settings > Privacy & Security (the app is not signed by Apple).
Copy the game folder and a memory dump of the running game (Minecraft for Windows 1.26.52) from a Windows PC, then open the app and point it at both.

Build from source: install Xcode with the Metal toolchain and the Homebrew packages listed in the README, then run ./setup.sh --game "/path/to/game/folder" --dump "/path/to/dump.dmp" (about 30 GB and 1-2 hours on first build).
Start the game with tools/play_minecraft.sh or by double-clicking Play Minecraft.command.
Optional: run scripts/build-app.sh to build the app and dist/Bedrock-Launcher.dmg.
notable: Runs the real Windows Bedrock game on Apple silicon without shipping any game files; the user supplies their own copy and a memory dump.
Rebuilds the encrypted game executable from a full memory dump, restoring its import table.
Includes an offline stand-in replacement for the game's HTTP library, which is how online features are disabled.
Launcher app packaged as a DMG, with setup.sh that builds the whole stack from source and skips completed steps on rerun.
Documents a reverse-engineering workflow in which AI agents traced and fixed each crash, according to the README.
caveats: Online features are unavailable: sign-in, Realms, Marketplace and multiplayer servers do not work.
Only Minecraft for Windows version 1.26.52 has been tested, and the tools' addresses match only that version; it requires Apple silicon and was tested on macOS 27.
Requires a legally owned Windows copy plus a memory dump, a large build (about 30 GB, 1-2 hours) for source builds, and the app is not signed by Apple so macOS blocks it on first launch.
summary.license: MIT for the scripts, tools and stubs (per LICENSE); patches in patches/wine-gdk fall under LGPL 2.1 and patches in patches/dxmt under MIT. The app bundles Wine, GnuTLS, Nettle, GMP, FreeType, DXMT and Python under their own licences.
